title: Quantum Rabi oscillations of a qubit strongly coupled to a one-dimensional waveguide
authors: Ya. S. Greenberg, A. A. Shtygashev, O. A. Chuikin, A. G. Moiseev, O. V. Kibis
abstract: We theoretically investigate quantum Rabi oscillations in a system consisting of a two-level atom (qubit) strongly coupled to a one-dimensional open waveguide. In contrast to conventional cavity quantum electrodynamics, the qubit interacts with a continuum of propagating modes, which gives rise to fundamentally different dynamical behavior. Within the rotating-wave approximation, we express the multimode Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian in terms of collective bosonic operators and show that the system possesses two integrals of motion, enabling an exact diagonalization of the Hamiltonian in the single-excitation subspace. Considering the initially excited qubit and field states described by multiphoton Fock-like states, we demonstrate that the Rabi oscillations represent a collective phenomenon corresponding to oscillations between multiphoton states differing by a single photon. We then extend our analysis to multiphoton processes in which the initial field is a multimode coherent state in a continuous spectrum. In this case, the Rabi frequency is shown to be sensitive to the spectral profile of the function that generates the coherent state.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes how a qubit undergoes Rabi oscillations when strongly coupled to the continuum modes of an open waveguide, moving beyond standard cavity QED models. The key finding is that the oscillation frequency depends critically on the spectral profile and loss rate of the waveguide environment. This highlights the fundamental role of dissipation in shaping coherent quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates quantum Rabi oscillations of a qubit strongly coupled to the continuum modes of an open one-dimensional waveguide, contrasting this behavior with conventional cavity QED.
main_result: Rabi oscillations are shown to be collective phenomena whose frequency is highly sensitive to the spectral profile and loss rate ($\gamma$) of the continuous waveguide spectrum, especially when initialized in a coherent state.
method: The analysis uses theoretical Hamiltonian methods, employing the rotating-wave approximation and diagonalizing the system's dynamics within specialized subspaces (single-excitation or collective operators).
model_or_system: The physical system is a two-level atom (qubit) coupled to a 1D waveguide continuum. The dynamics are governed by a multimode Jaynes-Cummings Hamiltonian, which allows for exact diagonalization in certain subspaces.
key_observables: Rabi frequency ($\Omega_R$), probability of qubit excitation ($P_e(t)$), and the average oscillation frequency $\langle\omegaangle$.
important_parameters: Mode loss rate ($\gamma = \Gamma/\Omega$) and detuning between qubit and mode frequencies ($x_0 = \omega_0/\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the rotating-wave approximation (RWA) and assumes specific functional forms for spectral profiles, such as Lorentzian or Gaussian shapes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of the average frequency $\langle\omegaangle$ and the Rabi frequency ($\Omega_R$) on the loss rate ($\gamma$) and detuning ($x_0$), demonstrating strong spectral dependence.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the Hamiltonian and integrals of motion, analyzing single-photon exchange dynamics, extending to multimode Fock states, and culminating in a detailed analysis of coherent state coupling in the continuum limit.
why_interesting: This work provides crucial theoretical insight into open quantum systems where dissipation is inherent. The sensitivity of Rabi oscillations to the spectral density moves beyond simple cavity models, which is vital for designing realistic quantum devices using waveguides or photonic structures.
